name: Reputation loss

subjectOf.text: Governance decisions such as network upgrades follow a simple vote that mints no reputation, yet reputation in the SDAO can still be lost through a governance vote because each vote follows the DEVxDAO MVPR logic moving from loosely coupled to tightly coupled voting.
subjectOf.abstract: Governance decisions, such as network upgrades, among others, follow a simple vote process in which no reputation is minted. However, reputation in the SDAO can be lost as a result of a governance vote as each vote follows the DEVxDAO MVPR logic via loosely coupled to tightly coupled voting.
subjectOf.citation: Wulf A. Kaal, Hybrid Secure Proof of Stake (2021). SSRN: https://ssrn.com/abstract=3931933
scope_conditions: SDAO governance votes on network upgrades

subjectOf.text: SPoS imposes a dual penalty that reduces financial stake and reputation at the same time, amplifying accountability by combining immediate tangible cost with long-term social consequence inside the validator community.
subjectOf.abstract: When combined with slashing, which simultaneously reduces both financial stake and reputation—a dual penalty unique to SPoS—this mechanism amplifies accountability by imposing immediate tangible costs and long-term social consequences within the validator community
subjectOf.citation: Wulf A. Kaal, Cryptographic Foundations and Interdisciplinary Dimensions of the Secure Proof of Stake (SPoS) Conse (2025). SSRN: https://ssrn.com/abstract=5225296
